review.why: The PR removes the redundant @authenticate(token_auth) decorator from DELETE /api/tokens because the revoke() function already reads and validates the token from the Authorization header itself, so authentication behavior is unchanged.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Removing @authenticate(token_auth) leaves revoke() without any authentication guard, so the endpoint crashes with 500 when the Authorization header is missing or invalid instead of returning the documented 401.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Removing @authenticate(token_auth) leaves revoke() without any authentication guard, so the endpoint crashes with 500 when the Authorization header is missing or invalid instead of returning the documented 401.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Removing @authenticate(token_auth) leaves revoke() without any authentication guard, so the endpoint crashes with 500 when the Authorization header is missing or invalid instead of returning the documented 401.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR removes the authentication decorator but the endpoint now returns 500 instead of 401 for missing or invalid tokens.

personas.goal: Create a post and view the feed

personas.name: bob_power
personas.goal: Follow alice, post multiple times, view following list

personas.name: carol_minimal
personas.goal: Login and view own profile only

personas.name: dave_spammer
personas.goal: Post empty text, post too long, post duplicate id attempt

personas.name: erin_edge
personas.goal: Post with non-starting-letter username probe, post with missing fields

personas.name: frank_testdel
personas.goal: Delete a post authored by another user (should fail 403)

personas.name: alice_follow_cycle
personas.goal: Follow then unfollow bob, verify state changes

personas.name: bob_feed_only
personas.goal: View feed with only followed user's posts

personas.name: carol_boundary
personas.goal: Post exactly 280 chars, post 1 char, post 281 chars

personas.name: dave_token_revoke
personas.goal: Login, get token, revoke it, verify 401 on next call

personas.name: probe s1: power_user_alice
personas.goal: Normal authenticated operations

personas.name: probe s2: careless_user_bob
personas.goal: Send invalid payloads to find validation gaps

personas.name: probe s3: power_user_carol
personas.goal: Full CRUD cycle then revoke

personas.name: round2 probe_s1_missing_auth
personas.goal: Test DELETE /api/tokens with no Authorization header to trigger suspicion s1 (401 with WWW-Authenticate: Form instead of Bearer).

personas.name: round2 probe_s2_invalid_token
personas.goal: Test DELETE /api/tokens with an invalid Bearer token to trigger suspicion s2 (401 with WWW-Authenticate: Form instead of Bearer).

personas.name: round2 probe_s3_revoked_token
personas.goal: Test DELETE /api/tokens with a valid JWT whose token record was revoked to trigger suspicion s3 (403 with WWW-Authenticate: Form instead of Bearer).

personas.name: round2 probe_s4_disable_auth_no_user1
personas.goal: Test DELETE /api/tokens with DISABLE_AUTH=true and user id=1 missing to trigger suspicion s4 (401 with WWW-Authenticate: Form instead of Bearer).

personas.name: round2 probe_s5_disable_auth_user1_no_password
personas.goal: Test DELETE /api/tokens with DISABLE_AUTH=true and user id=1 having no password_hash to trigger suspicion s5 (500 Internal Server Error).

personas.name: round2 probe_s6_valid_jwt_nonexistent_token_claim
personas.goal: Test DELETE /api/tokens with a valid JWT whose 'token' claim does not exist in tokens table to trigger suspicion s6 (500 Internal Server Error).

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens now returns 401 with a 'WWW-Authenticate: Form' header instead of the documented 'WWW-Authenticate: Bearer' header when the Authorization header is missing or malformed.
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/tokens with no Authorization header or with a malformed Authorization header (e.g., 'Authorization: Bearer' with no token). Read back the response status code and the WWW-Authenticate response header; observe a 401 status and a 'WWW-Authenticate: Form' header instead of the documented 'WWW-Authenticate: Bearer'.
suspicions.evidence: round2 probe_s1_missing_auth sent DELETE /api/tokens with no Authorization header; base returned 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, head returned 500 Internal Server Error, so the claimed Form header was not observed.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens now returns 401 with a 'WWW-Authenticate: Form' header instead of 'WWW-Authenticate: Bearer' when the Authorization header contains a valid Bearer scheme but the token is invalid or expired.
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/tokens with 'Authorization: Bearer <invalid_or_expired_token>'. Read back the response status code and the WWW-Authenticate response header; observe a 401 status and a 'WWW-Authenticate: Form' header instead of the documented 'WWW-Authenticate: Bearer'.
suspicions.evidence: round2 probe_s2_invalid_token sent DELETE /api/tokens with an invalid Bearer token; both base and head returned 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, so the claimed Form header does not occur.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens returns 403 with a 'WWW-Authenticate: Form' header instead of 'WWW-Authenticate: Bearer' when the access token is valid but the token record is missing from the database (e.g., revoked).
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/tokens with 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_jwt_but_revoked_token>'. Read back the response status code and the WWW-Authenticate response header; observe a 403 status and a 'WWW-Authenticate: Form' header instead of the documented 'WWW-Authenticate: Bearer'.
suspicions.evidence: round2 probe_s3_revoked_token obtained a token and deleted it twice (both 204), but never sent DELETE /api/tokens with a valid JWT whose token record is missing, so the trigger condition was not reached.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens returns 401 with a 'WWW-Authenticate: Form' header instead of 'WWW-Authenticate: Bearer' when DISABLE_AUTH=true and the seeded user (id=1) does not exist in the database.
suspicions.trigger: Set DISABLE_AUTH=true, ensure user id=1 does not exist in the database, then send DELETE /api/tokens with any Authorization header (or none). Read back the response status code and the WWW-Authenticate response header; observe a 401 status and a 'WWW-Authenticate: Form' header instead of the documented 'WWW-Authenticate: Bearer'.
suspicions.evidence: round2 probe_s4_disable_auth_no_user1 sent DELETE /api/tokens with DISABLE_AUTH=true and no user id=1; base returned 401, head returned 500 (change f1), showing a regression.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens returns 500 Internal Server Error when DISABLE_AUTH=true and the seeded user (id=1) exists but has no password_hash, because the token_auth decorator's error handler returns a tuple that Flask cannot convert to a response.
suspicions.trigger: Set DISABLE_AUTH=true, ensure user id=1 exists but has password_hash=NULL, then send DELETE /api/tokens with any Authorization header (or none). Read back the response status code; observe a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a 401 Unauthorized.
suspicions.evidence: round2 probe_s5_disable_auth_user1_no_password sent DELETE /api/tokens with DISABLE_AUTH=true and user id=1 lacking password_hash; base returned 401, head returned 500 (change f2), showing a regression.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/tokens returns 500 Internal Server Error when the Authorization header uses Bearer scheme with a valid JWT whose 'token' claim does not exist in the tokens table, because the token_auth decorator's error handler returns a tuple that Flask cannot convert to a response.
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/tokens with 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_jwt_with_nonexistent_token_claim>'. Read back the response status code; observe a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a 401 Unauthorized.
suspicions.evidence: round2 probe_s6_valid_jwt_nonexistent_token_claim obtained a valid token and deleted it twice (both 204), but never sent DELETE /api/tokens with a valid JWT whose token claim does not exist in the tokens table, so the trigger condition was not reached.
